purpose: Prospective baseline-absence gates for candidate existence cases. Each was rejected before extraction/source arms because the no-analogue planner already produced the exact hoped-for useful element.

probes.target: A startup cultures an oxygen-sensitive enzyme in sealed, opaque production cartridges. Opening a cartridge or withdrawing a sample admits enough oxygen to ruin that entire cartridge. The conversion endpoint varies from 6 to 14 hours with the room's thermal cycle, so the fixed-time release schedule has repeatedly released incomplete batches. Exterior instruments report jacket temperature and agitator speed, but none measures enzyme conversion. Each run's cartridges are filled from one well-mixed feed preparation, the processing rack has one unused cartridge slot, and losing one cartridge is acceptable if it prevents releasing the rest too early. The team must decide when to release each run without opening the production cartridges.
probes.hoped_for_element: co-process and destructively assay a sacrificial witness cartridge from the same feed

steps: Fill the rack's spare slot with a sacrificial witness cartridge from the same well-mixed feed, and process it alongside the production cartridges under the same rack conditions.

Use accumulated jacket-temperature exposure and agitator history to choose the earliest contemplated release time (never before 6 hours); then open only the witness and immediately run the validated conversion assay.
Record the witness result and the run conditions; keep every production cartridge sealed throughout.
baseline_output.release_rule: Release all production cartridges immediately only if the sacrificial witness meets the predefined conversion-endpoint specification. If it fails, do not release early; continue the sealed production cartridges to 14 hours and release only under a validated rule that establishes 14 hours as sufficient within the allowed operating envelope.
assumptions: A witness filled from the same well-mixed preparation and placed in the same rack is representative of the production cartridges.
Opening the witness permits a rapid, reliable endpoint assay of conversion achieved up to that moment, even though oxygen subsequently ruins that witness.

The observed 6-to-14-hour range has been validated as a hard bound for the permitted temperature and agitation envelope; otherwise a failed witness requires quarantine rather than automatic release at 14 hours.

probes.target: An online ledger has frozen writes to several key ranges while corruption is repaired. The repair coordinator assigns a range to a worker. A worker may split its range and hand a subrange to another worker, which may hand it on again. Workers can report their own repair complete independently. Writes arriving during the freeze are retained in per-range delta logs. Produce a plan for reopening each range without admitting a write while repair or replay work on that range is still under way.
probes.hoped_for_element: reopen only when the transitive delegation tree has zero active repair descendants and replay is drained

steps: For each frozen range and freeze epoch, have the coordinator track a delegation tree plus counters for every active repair and replay task; splitting registers the child atomically before the parent can report completion, and completion removes only that task, never its descendants.

Keep write admission closed and append every arriving write to that range's ordered, epoch-tagged delta log while any repair task in the full delegation tree remains active; require terminal acknowledgement (or coordinator-resolved failure/reassignment) for every descendant.

After repair quiescence, start a tracked replay task and replay deltas idempotently in order while new arrivals continue to be logged; repeat draining until an atomic cutover can lock both write admission and delta-log append.
Under that cutover lock, re-evaluate the guard; only if it is true atomically mark the range open, otherwise release the lock still frozen and resume repair/replay.
baseline_output.reopen_guard: under range_cutover_lock: range.freeze_epoch == epoch && range.state == FROZEN && active_repair_tasks_in_transitive_delegation_tree(range, epoch) == 0 && active_replay_tasks(range, epoch) == 0 && delta_log(range, epoch).is_empty()

probes.target: A university is containing a malware incident across 10,000 laptops. Its endpoint detector flagged 120 machines and its DNS-anomaly detector independently flagged 80; 30 machines appear on both lists. Confirmed spot checks show that each detector misses some infected machines. Re-running either detector produces nearly the same list, and no third detection tool can be deployed this week. Keeping every department isolated much longer will stop payroll and registration. The response team must estimate how many infected laptops neither detector found and set a defensible condition for reconnecting departments.
probes.hoped_for_element: use two-source capture-recapture to estimate infections missed by both detectors

steps.action: Freeze and deduplicate the two current lists: 170 distinct laptops are detected (120 + 80 - 30). Immediately isolate and remediate those 170; do not treat detector reruns as new independent samples.

Use two-source capture-recapture for campus-wide planning. The Chapman estimate is ((120+1)*(80+1)/(30+1))-1 = 315 infected laptops total, so about 145 infected laptops are unseen. A model-based approximate 95% profile-likelihood range is 258-421 total, or 88-251 unseen. This requires a closed population, conditional detector independence, and roughly equal detection probability; report the assumptions with the estimate.

After removing detected machines, draw a fresh random validation sample within each department from its unflagged laptops using the existing forensic spot-check process. Test 299 laptops, or every unflagged laptop if fewer than 299; any confirmed infection triggers continued isolation, remediation, and a new fresh sample.

unseen_infections_estimate.basis: Chapman two-source capture-recapture; 170 infections are already represented in the union

baseline_output.reconnect_rule: Reconnect a department only after every laptop flagged by either detector is removed or verified remediated and a fresh random sample of 299 unflagged laptops (or all of them if fewer than 299) contains zero infections. Zero positives in 299 gives a one-sided 95% upper bound below 1% for residual prevalence; if any positive is found, keep that department isolated, remediate, and restart validation with a fresh sample.

probes.target:
A national LPG regulator has found counterfeit pressure-relief valves on an unknown subset of 18,000 refillable household gas cylinders. A bad valve can rupture during filling. Cylinders continually move among households and 43 licensed refill depots. Painted serial numbers are often illegible or duplicated, ownership changes informally, and there is no complete inventory or trustworthy owner registry. The regulator therefore cannot enumerate the affected cylinders.

All legal refilling passes through the 43 depots, whose compliance can be audited. Depot staff have about five seconds per cylinder and no reliable network connection. Six service centers can inspect or replace 500 valves per day each. The regulator can prepare 2,000 known-safe cylinders before launch, but cannot suspend LPG service for more than 48 hours. Some unused cylinders may not be presented for months.

Give exactly six prioritized operational actions for an eight-week response that maintains household access, removes unsafe cylinders from circulation, and prevents an old, uninspected cylinder from re-entering later. Do not assume that the cylinders can first be enumerated or that a new electronic registry can be made reliable.
probes.hoped_for_element: blanket-retire old cylinder markings and enforce permanent no-new-marker/no-refill at all depots with inward exchange

actions.action: Issue an emergency national refill rule and one physical certification standard: after a single coordinated activation time, every depot must refuse to connect or fill any cylinder lacking an intact regulator-issued, tamper-evident collar or seal that is destroyed if the valve is removed. The five-second decision is marker intact equals eligible to fill; absent, damaged, or doubtful equals quarantine. Painted serials, ownership records, and network lookups are not used.

Certify and mark the 2,000 known-safe cylinders, allocate them across all 43 depots using expected demand with minimum contingency stock at each, and give each depot a paper quick-reference card, quarantine cage, receipts, and deposit-neutral exchange authority. Train and observe every filling crew on the stop-before-connection check; keep any line-conversion pause below 48 hours.

Run mandatory access-preserving exchange at the refill chokepoint: an unmarked cylinder is never filled, is accepted into controlled quarantine, and the household immediately receives a filled certified cylinder from the pool without an ownership or serial-number dispute. An intact marked cylinder follows normal refill practice. Isolate leaking or damaged cylinders under hazardous-goods procedures rather than placing them in the ordinary cage.

Operate scheduled sealed-cage shuttles from every depot to the six service centers and return certified cylinders on the reverse route. At a center, replace an unmarked valve with controlled genuine stock unless an approved inspection conclusively verifies it, then leak/pressure-test the cylinder, condemn unsafe shells, and crimp the tamper-evident certification marker onto the valve assembly. Use the combined 3,000-per-day capacity to keep turnaround under one day where possible, replenish depot exchange stocks first, and rebalance the 2,000-cylinder buffer daily.

Control diversion and noncompliance with offline chain-of-custody and field audits: each depot and shuttle keeps signed paper counts of unmarked cylinders accepted, certified cylinders issued, quarantined stock, center receipts, returned stock, and condemned units. Regulator teams perform unannounced fill-line observation and physical count reconciliation at all 43 depots, immediately stop any bypassing line, sanction unauthorized filling, and investigate missing seals or count discrepancies; reporting may later be uploaded but operations do not depend on it.

Publicize a simple nationwide message through dealers, radio, and cylinder stickers: bring any cylinder to a licensed depot for a free immediate safe exchange, do not seek informal filling, and report leaks. Conduct targeted mobile collection/exchange days in low-turnover areas during Weeks 3-8, but retain the no-intact-marker/no-fill rule, exchange facility, seal supply control, and audit check indefinitely so a cylinder unused for months is intercepted whenever it eventually returns.

baseline_output.safety_invariant: No cylinder without an intact regulator-issued certification marker is ever connected to filling equipment or repressurized; service continuity for its holder is provided only by exchanging it for a certified cylinder, while the suspect cylinder remains in controlled custody until certified or condemned.
assumptions: The regulator can mandate depot procedures, authorize deposit-neutral cylinder exchange, and sanction violations.
All legal refilling continues to pass through the 43 auditable depots, so indefinite enforcement at that chokepoint captures late-presenting cylinders without enumerating them.
Approved genuine valves, tamper-evident markers, hazardous-goods transport, and enough filled LPG product are available to use the stated service-center capacity.
Certification includes shell-condition and leak/pressure checks required by existing cylinder safety rules; a marker is not applied to a cylinder that fails them.

probes.target: A team is fuzz-testing a new binary protocol parser before release. Crash inputs are replayed and canonicalized into distinct underlying failure signatures. So far the campaign has found 100 distinct failure signatures: 40 signatures appeared in exactly one test input, 10 appeared in exactly two inputs, and the other 50 appeared at least three times. Recent batches still add previously unseen singleton signatures. Branch coverage has plateaued, but past parser releases reached the same coverage while still containing serious undiscovered failure modes. The team has only this one fuzzer and must decide whether the observed signature counts support release or imply that many failure classes remain undiscovered.
probes.hoped_for_element: use singleton/doubleton Chao1 estimation to quantify undiscovered failure classes

baseline_output.calculation: Using the Chao1 unseen-class lower-bound estimator with S_obs=100, f1=40 singletons, and f2=10 doubletons: unseen = f1^2/(2*f2) = 40^2/(2*10) = 80. This implies at least about 180 total failure classes and only about 56% observed; continuing new singletons indicates the campaign is not saturated.
baseline_output.decision: Do not treat these counts or plateaued branch coverage as supporting release. They imply many undiscovered failure classes remain, and the coverage plateau is not persuasive given prior releases with serious failures at the same coverage.
next_steps: Continue the campaign rather than release, allocating a defined additional fuzzing budget and tracking f1, f2, and the Chao1 estimate after each batch.
Retune the existing fuzzer with seeds and protocol-aware dictionaries or mutations derived from rare-signature inputs to reach new parser states.
Reassess release only after new-signature discovery and the unseen-class estimate materially decline across multiple consecutive batches.
